newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Captall eyes Southern Life - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Captall eyes Southern Life - newspaper.

text.p: JOHANNESBURG, June 22 (Reuter) South Africa's Capital Alliance financial services group is believed to be close to buying a controlling share in life assurer Southern Life Association Ltd, the Sunday Times newspaper reported.
The Johannesburg-based newspaper said in its Business Times section that Capital Alliance (Captall) chief executive Mark Barnes and Southern Life officials had declined to comment on the speculation.

But the newspaper quoted market analysts as saying the booming Captall group, with interests from financial services to mining, could take Anglo American Corp's 32 percent stake in Southern as well as First National Bank's 29.5 percent holding.
The newspaper said First National's stake in Southern was worth about 5.3 billion rand while Southern held a 25 percent stake in the bank worth an estimated 4.2 billion rand.
Barnes told investors early in June that his group, with earnings per share up to 102.4 cents in the year to April from 52.9 cents, would continue to seek new acquisitions.
On June 5, Captall bought the entire business operations of Financial Services Corp (Pty) Ltd (Fincorp) for an undisclosed amount.
Other recent acquisitions have included the former NDH Bank, now Capital Alliance Bank, Seeff Holdings and a 60 percent interest in Global Capital.
Barnes said recently he expected to increase assets under management fourfold from 1.2 billion rand within months.
Southern reported total assets of 32.6 billion rand in May, when it released disappointing results that saw the share price fall eight percent to 41 rand in a day.
